## Introduction

This document provides examples of the main theoretical tools available in **ARMA Theory**.

The library works with user-specified AR and MA coefficients and studies the population properties implied by those coefficients.

## Setup

```{python}
import arma_theory as arma
```

## A first ARMA model

Consider an ARMA(1,1) model with

$$
y_t = 0.8y_{t-1} + \varepsilon_t + 0.5\varepsilon_{t-1}.
$$

The corresponding Python coefficients are:

```{python}
ar = [0.8]
ma = [0.5]
```

We can examine the basic polynomial diagnostics:

```{python}
diagnostics = arma.arma_diagnostics(ar=ar, ma=ma)

print("Causal:", diagnostics["causal"])
print("Invertible:", diagnostics["invertible"])
```
